questions.stem: What problem is Britain facing?
options: A) The number of nurses has dropped to a record low.
B) There is a growing shortage of medical personnel.
C) There is discrimination against male nurses.
D) The number of male nurses has gone down.

explain.定位:
Figures show the number of male nurses has fallen in the last three years.
数据显示，过去三年里男护士的数量一直在下降。
explain.信号:
Figures show 引出的事实陈述句。新闻开篇先发出呼吁，紧接着用 Figures show the
number of male nurses has fallen in the last three years. 摆出数据事实——"数据显
示"这类引出客观事实的句子，往往就是新闻交代核心状况的答案句。
explain.替换:
the number of male nurses has fallen ↔ The number of male nurses has gone down.
fallen 同义换成 gone down
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
原文确有 has reached a seven-year low（七年来最低），选项 The number of nurses
has dropped to a record low. 借这个 low 字诱你选，但 record low 是"史上最低"，七年
低≠创纪录最低，程度被偷偷拔高，且原文讲的是 male nurses 而非笼统 nurses。
借用原文：reached a seven-year low
B) 偷换概念
原文只说 the number of male nurses has fallen，是男护士这一群体减少；There is a
growing shortage of medical personnel. 把范围放大成整个 medical personnel 短缺，
属于偷换概念、扩大范围，原文从没说整体医护短缺。
借用原文：the number of male nurses has fallen
C) 未提及
There is discrimination against male nurses. 听起来与男护士相关，但原文只讲数量下降
和这是 a cultural problem，从未说存在"歧视"；把 cultural problem 脑补成
discrimination 是过度推断，原文无此说法。

questions.stem: What is the cause of the problem according to the UK Health Secretary?

explain.定位:
The UK Health Secretary said, "This is clearly a cultural problem, and probably one that
exists in many parts of the world."
英国卫生大臣说："这显然是一个文化问题，可能在世界许多地方都存在。"
explain.信号:
Health Secretary said 后的直接归因。题干限定 according to the UK Health
Secretary，原文正好出现 The UK Health Secretary said, "This is clearly a cultural
problem——指定人物开口、又用 clearly 加重语气下判断，这种"某人说+明确归因"的句
子就是答案句。
explain.替换:
This is clearly a cultural problem ↔ Cultural bias.
cultural problem 概括为 cultural bias
explain.排除:
B) 未提及
Inadequate pay. 是生活常识里最顺的离职理由，极易凭印象选；但卫生大臣只说这是 a
cultural problem，全篇没提 pay 或工资，属未提及、用常识替原文。
C) 未提及
Educational system. 听上去也像合理原因，但原文把原因明确归为 a cultural problem，
从未提教育体制，属未提及。
D) 未提及
Working conditions. 又是一个常识里顺手的理由，但原文唯一的归因是 a cultural
problem，没提工作条件，属未提及。
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 A man from Libya was enjoying a walk along the sands at Southport Beach. When he was about half
a mile out from the dock, he felt a bit tired. So he lay down and fell asleep. But the tide swept in
quickly at the beach. And the man was shocked to wake up and find the tide had come in and
completely surrounded him, cutting him off from the shore. Fortunately for him, the beach lifeguards
were quickly on the scene to stop him from drowning. They acted professionally to ensure the man was
comfortable until an ambulance arrived. He was then taken to hospital. He is now in a stable condition.
When interviewed, Keith Porter of the Southport Beach said, "Our beach is so flat that it's very common
for the tide to come around the back of people and cut them off from the beach. Thankfully the
emergency services have again worked well together to ensure a positive outcome. And we wish the
gentleman a speedy recovery."
一名来自利比亚的男子正在Southport海滩的沙滩上散步。当他走到离码头约半英里的地方时，他感到有
点累。于是他躺下来睡着了。但海滩上的潮水迅速涌入。这名男子震惊地醒来，发现潮水已经涨起来并完
全包围了他，使他与岸边隔绝。幸运的是，海滩救生员迅速赶到现场，阻止他溺水。他们专业地行动，确
保这名男子在救护车到达之前感到舒适。随后他被送往医院。他现在情况稳定。在接受采访时，
Southport海滩的Keith Porter说："我们的海滩非常平坦，潮水绕到人们身后并将他们与海滩隔开是很常
见的。值得庆幸的是，应急服务部门再次通力合作，确保了积极的结果。我们祝愿这位先生早日康复。"

questions.stem: What does the news report say about the Libyan man?
options: A) He fell out of a lifeboat.
B) He lost his way on a beach.
D) He enjoyed swimming in the sea.

explain.定位:
Fortunately for him, the beach lifeguards were quickly on the scene to stop him
from drowning.
对他来说幸运的是，海滩救生员迅速赶到现场，阻止了他溺水。
explain.信号:
stop him from drowning 点出险情。答案句的信号是险情结果短语：to stop him from
drowning，加上前文 the tide had come in and completely surrounded him, cutting
him off from the shore 描述他被潮水包围、与岸隔绝，两句合起来说明他险些溺水、被及
时阻止。
explain.替换:
to stop him from drowning ↔ He was almost drowned.
阻止溺水=差点溺水
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
选项说他 fell out of a lifeboat（从救生艇掉下），录音里出现的是 the beach lifeguards
（救生员），二者发音相近，借此诱你听到类似词就选；但原文是救生员来救他，他从没在
救生艇上，更没掉下来。
借用原文：the beach lifeguards were quickly on the scene
B) 未提及
选项说他 lost his way on a beach（在海滩迷路），录音从头到尾说的是他累了睡着、被
潮水包围，没有任何迷路情节，属凭海滩场景臆造。
D) 偷换概念
选项说他 enjoyed swimming in the sea（享受海里游泳），录音里他是 enjoying a walk
along the sands（享受沙滩散步）后躺下睡着，并非游泳。选项盗用 enjoying 这个原词并
把散步偷换成游泳，制造听到 enjoy 就选的诱惑。
借用原文：enjoying a walk along the sands

questions.stem: What did Keith Porter say at an interview?
options: A) The beach is a popular tourist resort.
B) The emergency services are efficient.
C) The beach is a good place to watch the tide.
D) The lifeboats patrol the area round the clock.

explain.定位:
Thankfully the emergency services have again worked well together to ensure a
positive outcome.
幸好，应急部门又一次通力协作，确保了一个好结果。
explain.信号:
引语中的正向评价句。答案句是 Keith Porter 原话引语里的表态部分：the emergency
services have again worked well together，由 Thankfully 领起、带明显肯定色彩，是受
访者对救援的评价落点，正是评价题要抓的表态句。
explain.替换:
the emergency services have again worked well together ↔ The emergency services are efficient.
通力协作=高效
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
选项说海滩是 popular tourist resort（热门旅游景点），录音里 Keith Porter 只说 Our
beach is so flat（我们海滩很平坦），从没说它是热门景点。选项借 beach 这个反复出现
的词，硬安一个采访里没有的评价。
借用原文：Our beach is so flat
C) 原词陷阱
选项说海滩是 good place to watch the tide（看潮好去处），录音里 tide 出现于 it's
very common for the tide to come around the back of people and cut them off，讲
的是潮水危险地切断人的退路，而非适合观潮。选项盗用核心词 tide，把危险偷换成了好去
处。
借用原文：it's very common for the tide to come around the back of people and cut them off from
the beach
D) 未提及
选项说救生艇 patrol the area round the clock（全天候巡逻），录音里 Keith Porter 只说
救生员 quickly on the scene（迅速赶到），从未提到全天候巡逻。round the clock 这种
绝对程度表述是录音没有的添加。

questions.stem: What does the news report say about the raccoon, a small cat-like animal?
options: A) It became an online star.
B) It broke into an office room.
C) It escaped from a local zoo.
D) It climbed 25 storeys at one go.

explain.定位:
It was captured after becoming an online star across the world.
它在成为风靡全球的网络明星之后被抓住了。
explain.信号:
becoming an online star 直陈事实。答案句靠的是直接陈述这一事实信号：becoming
an online star across the world 平铺直叙地说浣熊“成了全球网红”，正对应选项 A 要核对
的那件事，不需转折也不需推断，听到 star 就该锁定。
explain.替换:
becoming an online star across the world ↔ It became an online star.
几乎原句压缩
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
选项 It broke into an office room. 盗用了原文 office tower（办公大楼）里的 office 一
词，制造“听到 office 就想选”的诱惑，但原文只说浣熊在大楼外墙往上爬、停在窗沿，从没
说它“闯进办公室”。
借用原文：spotted stuck on a narrow window edge of the office tower
C) 未提及
选项 It escaped from a local zoo. 给了一个“从动物园逃跑”的来历，听起来很合理，但通
篇原文只说它是 a small cat-like animal、爬楼、被放归野外，从未提及任何动物园或它如
何逃出，属凭常识脑补的来历。
D) 原词陷阱
选项 It climbed 25 storeys at one go. 用对了原文数字 25-storey skyscraper，但偷加了
at one go（一口气）。原文明说它中途 took a long break on a 17th floor window
edge、且爬楼跨了周一到周三好几天，根本不是一次爬完。
借用原文：took a long break on a 17th floor window edge

questions.stem: What will the wildlife management company do with the captured raccoon?
options: A) Send it back to the zoo.
B) Release it into the wild.
C) Return it to its owner.
D) Give it a physical checkup.

explain.定位:
A private wildlife management company will release the animal into the wild.
一家私人野生动物管理公司将把这只动物放归野外。
explain.信号:
主语 company 后跟 will release。题干主语 A private wildlife management company
在原文一出现，紧跟的动词 will release the animal into the wild 就是处置去向，这种“主
角 + 将做某事”的句式本身就是答案信号，听到该公司名就该准备记动词。
explain.替换:
release the animal into the wild ↔ Release it into the wild.
近乎原词对应
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
选项 Send it back to the zoo. 顺着第 5 题里“动物园”的常识联想编出“送回动物园”，但原
文根本没提动物园，处置去向写得清清楚楚是放归野外，不是送回。
C) 未提及
选项 Return it to its owner. 假设浣熊有主人、要“物归原主”，但这是野生浣熊，原文从头
到尾没有任何 owner（主人），处置也是放归野外，不存在归还。
D) 未提及
选项 Give it a physical checkup. 听起来“抓到动物理应先体检”很合理，但原文对处置只说
了 release the animal into the wild，从未提任何检查或体检，属凭常识替原文做主。

questions.stem: What did one online post say?
options: A) A raccoon can perform acts no human can.
B) A raccoon can climb much higher than a cat.
C) The raccoon became as famous as some politicians.
D) The raccoon did something no politician could.

explain.定位:
One online post said that the raccoon has succeeded in uniting the country the way no
politician could.
一条网帖说，这只浣熊成功地以一种没有任何政客能做到的方式团结了整个国家。
explain.信号:
said that 引出网帖原话。信号词 One online post said that 直接引出题干要的那句网帖
原话，said that 后面整句就是答案承载句；末尾 the way no politician could 是这句的落
点，必须听到尾巴才不被前半句带偏。
explain.替换:
uniting the country the way no politician could ↔
The raccoon did something no politician could.
团结全国 = 政客做不到的事
explain.排除:
A) 偷换概念
选项 A raccoon can perform acts no human can. 仿照原文 no politician could 的句
式，却把比较对象 politician（政客）偷换成 human（人类）。原文比的是政客、不是泛指
人类，对象一换意思就变了。
借用原文：the way no politician could
B) 原词陷阱
选项 A raccoon can climb much higher than a cat. 借用了原文形容浣熊是 a small cat-
like animal（像猫的小动物）里的 cat，编出“比猫爬得高”的比较，但原文从没拿浣熊和猫
比爬高，cat 只是用来描述它长相。
借用原文：a small cat-like animal
C) 偷换概念
选项 The raccoon became as famous as some politicians. 也保留了 politician，但把原
文的“做到了政客做不到的事”偷改成“和政客一样有名”。原文的落点是“政客办不到”（强调超
越），不是“名气相当”，意思被换掉了。
借用原文：the way no politician could

questions.stem: Why did the woman feel excited?
options: A) She got a well-paying job in a bank.
B) She received a bonus unexpectedly.
C) She received her first monthly salary.
D) She got a pay raise for her performance.

explain.定位:
So this is the first time I've ever been paid for a month of full-time work.
所以这是我第一次因为一整个月的全职工作而拿到工资。
explain.信号:
总结词 So 引出的结论句。女方先铺垫上学时只做兼职，再用 So this is the first time I've
ever been paid for a month of full-time work. 收口，So 这个『所以』把前面的铺垫归
结成结论——这一句正是她兴奋的真正原因。
explain.替换:
the first time I've ever been paid for a month of full-time work ↔
received her first monthly salary
『第一次拿到整月全职工资』= 『收到第一份月薪』
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音开头女方提到 I just got a text message from my bank，She got a well-paying job
in a bank. 就借这个 bank 来骗你——可那只是『银行发来短信通知工资到账』，根本没说
她在银行找了高薪工作，听到 bank 就选正中圈套。
借用原文：I just got a text message from my bank
B) 未提及
She received a bonus unexpectedly. 说的是『意外收到奖金』，但全程女方说的是 first
time…paid、salary，从没提 bonus，也没有『意外』之意，属录音根本没说的内容。
D) 偷换概念
She got a pay raise for her performance. 听起来也合理，但录音是『第一次拿全职工
资』，是头一回拿钱、不是『涨工资』，更没提 performance（表现）这个原因，把『第
一次拿』偷换成了『加薪』。

questions.stem: When did the man get his first full-time job?

explain.定位:
I mean, it's been two decades, but I can still remember when I got my first real salary.
我是说，都已经二十年了，但我还记得自己拿到第一笔真正的工资时的情形。
explain.信号:
时间数字 two decades。男方说 it's been two decades, but I can still remember when
I got my first real salary，two decades 就是直接的时间信号——距他第一份真正的工资
已过去二十年，时间锚点就在这个数字上。
explain.替换:
it's been two decades ↔ Two decades ago
『已经二十年了』= 『二十年前』
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
Several years ago. 是『几年前』，但男方说的是 two decades（二十年），several years
太短，对不上这个量级。
C) 张冠李戴
Right after graduation. 的『毕业后』对应的是女方那句 I worked all through university
（上学期间打工），而题问的是男方第一份全职工作的时间，把女方的上学经历安到男方头
上。
借用原文：I worked all through university
D) 张冠李戴
Just last month. 的『上个月』指向女方刚到账的这笔工资，而男方的第一份工资是 two
decades 前；把女方眼下的时间错当成男方过去的时间。

questions.stem: What did the man do when he got his first pay?
options: A) He sent a small check to his parents.
B) He took a few of his friends to a gym.
C) He immediately deposited it in a bank.
D) He treated his parents to a nice meal.

explain.定位:
I bought a new suit for work and took my parents to a nice restaurant to celebrate.
我买了一套上班穿的新西装，还带父母去了一家不错的餐厅庆祝。
explain.信号:
男方对『你拿钱做了啥』的直接应答。上一句女方问 What did you do with your first
pay?，男方紧接着用 I bought a new suit for work and took my parents to a nice
restaurant to celebrate. 作答——被问者的直接应答就是答案句所在。
explain.替换:
took my parents to a nice restaurant ↔ treated his parents to a nice meal
『带父母去好餐厅』= 『请父母吃顿好饭』
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
He sent a small check to his parents. 借了录音里的 parents 来骗你，但男方对父母做的
是『带去吃饭』，不是『寄支票』，parents 是真的、动作是假的。
借用原文：took my parents to a nice restaurant
B) 张冠李戴
He took a few of his friends to a gym. 里的 gym 来自后面 some people from the
office are members of a gym I want to join，那是女方要做的事、且是健身房不是『带朋
友去』，跟男方拿第一份工资做了什么无关。
借用原文：some people from the office are members of a gym I want to join
C) 原词陷阱
He immediately deposited it in a bank. 又拿 bank 来诱选，但男方说的是买西装、请父
母吃饭，全程没提把钱『存进银行』，是录音没有的动作。
借用原文：I just got a text message from my bank

questions.stem: What does the woman say she is going to do?
options: C) Join her colleagues for gym exercise.
D) Visit her former university campus.

explain.定位:
If I were you, I'd join the gym, because it's a good way to stay healthy... Hmm. You're right.

说得对，谢谢你的建议，我听你的。

建议句 + 女方收尾接受。男方先给建议 If I were you, I'd join the gym，女方最后用
Thanks for the advice. I'm taking it. 表态接受——『接受建议』这句收尾才是她真正决定
要做的事，落点在最后一句。

I'd join the gym ↔ Join her colleagues for gym exercise
『加入那个健身房』= 『和同事一起去健身房锻炼』
I'm taking it ↔ Join her colleagues for gym exercise
『我听你的』= 采纳『去健身房』这个建议
explain.排除:
A) 与原文相反
Buy some professional clothes. 借了男方建议里的『买正装』和女方话里的 professional
clothes，但女方明说 I have enough professional clothes.（我职业装够了），是被她否
掉的事，不是要做的。
借用原文：I have enough professional clothes.
B) 未提及
Budget her salary carefully. 说『仔细规划工资』，但对话里只说她钱不够、两件事只能选

Visit her former university campus. 对应 my university classmates are arranging a
trip to visit our old campus，她确实想去，但两件事 I can't afford both.，最后接受建议
选了健身房，回母校是被舍弃的一项。

questions.stem: Why does the man seem to be distracted?
options: A) He has a difficult decision to make.
B) He has been overworked recently.
C) He has just quarreled with his girlfriend.
D) He has just too many things to attend to.

我好像没法专注于任何事,因为我还没决定到底是接受伦敦那个博士项目的录取,还是接受纽
约那份工作。

the job offer in New York
↔ a difficult decision to make

questions.passage:
Is Breakfast Really the Most Important Meal of the Day?

A) Along with old classics like "carrots give you night vision" and "Santa doesn't bring toys to misbehaving children", one of the most well-worn phrases of tired parents everywhere is that breakfast is the most important meal of the day. Many of us grow up believing that skipping breakfast is a serious mistake, even if only two thirds of adults in the UK eat breakfast regularly, according to the British Dietetic Association, and around three-quarters of Americans.

B) "The body uses a lot of energy stores for growth and repair through the night," explains diet specialist Sarah Elder. "Eating a balanced breakfast helps to up our energy, as well as make up for protein and calcium used throughout the night." But there's widespread disagreement over whether breakfast should keep its top spot in the hierarchy(等级) of meals. There have been concerns around the sugar content of cereal and the food industry's involvement in pro-breakfast research—and even one claim from an academic that breakfast is "dangerous".

C) What's the reality? Is breakfast a necessary start to the day or a marketing tactic by cereal companies? The most researched aspect of breakfast (and breakfast-skipping) has been its links to obesity. Scientists have different theories as to why there's a relationship between the two. In one US study that analysed the health data of 50,000 people over seven years, researchers found that those who made breakfast the largest meal of the day were more likely to have a lower body mass index (BMI) than those who ate a large lunch or dinner. The researchers argued that breakfast helps reduce daily calorie intake and improve the quality of our diet—since breakfast foods are often higher in fibre and nutrients.

D) But as with any study of this kind, it was unclear if that was the cause—or if breakfast-skippers were just more likely to be overweight to begin with. questions.stem: To keep oneself healthy, eating breakfast is more important than choosing what to eat.
questions.passage:
Is Breakfast Really the Most Important Meal of the Day?

A) Along with old classics like "carrots give you night vision" and "Santa doesn't bring toys to misbehaving children", one of the most well-worn phrases of tired parents everywhere is that breakfast is the most important meal of the day. Many of us grow up believing that skipping breakfast is a serious mistake, even if only two thirds of adults in the UK eat breakfast regularly, according to the British Dietetic Association, and around three-quarters of Americans.

B) "The body uses a lot of energy stores for growth and repair through the night," explains diet specialist Sarah Elder. "Eating a balanced breakfast helps to up our energy, as well as make up for protein and calcium used throughout the night." But there's widespread disagreement over whether breakfast should keep its top spot in the hierarchy(等级) of meals. There have been concerns around the sugar content of cereal and the food industry's involvement in pro-breakfast research—and even one claim from an academic that breakfast is "dangerous".

C) What's the reality? Is breakfast a necessary start to the day or a marketing tactic by cereal companies? The most researched aspect of breakfast (and breakfast-skipping) has been its links to obesity. Scientists have different theories as to why there's a relationship between the two. In one US study that analysed the health data of 50,000 people over seven years, researchers found that those who made breakfast the largest meal of the day were more likely to have a lower body mass index (BMI) than those who ate a large lunch or dinner. The researchers argued that breakfast helps reduce daily calorie intake and improve the quality of our diet—since breakfast foods are often higher in fibre and nutrients.

D) But as with any study of this kind, it was unclear if that was the cause—or if breakfast-skippers were just more likely to be overweight to begin with. To find out, researchers designed a study in which 52 obese women took part in a 12-week weight loss programme. All had the same number of calories over the day, but half had breakfast, while the other half did not. What they found was that it wasn't breakfast itself that caused the participants to lose weight: it was changing their normal routine.

E) If breakfast alone isn't a guarantee of weight loss, why is there a link between obesity and breakfast-skipping? Alexandra Johnstone, professor of appetite research at the University of Aberdeen, argues that it may simply be because breakfast-skippers have been found to be less knowledgeable about nutrition and health. "There are a lot of studies on the relationship between breakfast eating and possible health outcomes, but this may be because those who eat breakfast choose to habitually have health-enhancing behaviours such as regular exercise and not smoking," she says.

F) A 2016 review of 10 studies looking into the relationship between breakfast and weight management concluded there is "limited evidence" supporting or refuting(反驳) the argument that breakfast influences weight or food intake, and more evidence is required before breakfast recommendations can be used to help prevent obesity.

G) Researchers from the University of Surrey and University of Aberdeen are halfway through research looking into the mechanisms behind how the time we eat influences body weight. Early findings suggest that a bigger breakfast is beneficial to weight control. Breakfast has been found to affect more than just weight. Skipping breakfast has been associated with a 27% increased risk of heart disease, a 21% higher risk of type 2 diabetes in men, and a 20% higher risk of type 2 diabetes in women. One reason may be breakfast's nutritional value partly because cereal is fortified(增加营养价值) with vitamins. In one study on the breakfast habits of 1,600 young people in the UK, researchers found that the fibre and micronutrient intake was better in those who had breakfast regularly. There have been similar findings in Australia, Brazil, Canada and the US.

H) Breakfast is also associated with improved brain function, including concentration and language use. A review of 54 studies found that eating breakfast can improve memory, though the effects on other brain functions were inconclusive. However, one of the review's researchers, Mary Beth Spitznagel, says there is "reasonable" evidence breakfast does improve concentration—there just needs to be more research. "Looking at studies that tested concentration the number of studies showing a benefit was exactly the same as the number that found no benefit," she says. "And no studies found that eating breakfast was bad for concentration."

I) What's most important, some argue, is what we eat for breakfast. High-protein breakfasts have been found particularly effective in reducing the longing for food and consumption later in the day, according to research by the Australian Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation. While cereal remains a firm favourite among breakfast consumers in the UK and US, a recent investigation into the sugar content of 'adult' breakfast cereals found that "some cereals contain more than three-quarters of the recommended daily amount of free sugars in each portion, and sugar was the second or third highest ingredient in cereals."

J) But some research suggests if we're going to eat sugary foods, it's best to do it early. One study recruited 200 obese adults to take part in a 16-week-long diet, where half added dessert to their breakfast, and half didn't. Those who added dessert lost an average of 40 pounds more—however, the study was unable to show the long-term effects. "Breakfast is most important for people who are hungry when they wake up," Johnstone says. "Each body starts the day differently—and those individual differences need to be researched more closely," Spitznagel says. "A balanced breakfast is really helpful, but getting regular meals throughout the day is more important to leave blood sugar stable through the day, which helps control weight and hunger levels," says Elder. questions.stem: What is the distinctive feature of a sea slug?

B) It lives half on animals and half on plants.
C) It converts some sea animals into plants.

questions.passage:
When we think of animals and plants, we have a pretty good way of dividing them into two distinct groups: one converts sunlight into energy and the other has to eat food to make its energy. Well, those dividing lines come crashing down with the discovery of a sea slug(海姑蛹) that's truly half animal and half plant. It's pretty incredible how it has managed to hijack the genes of the algae(藻类) on which it feeds.

The slugs can manufacture chlorophyll, the green pigment(色素) in plants that captures energy from sunlight, and hold these genes within their body. The term kleptoplasty is used to describe the practice of using hijacked genes to create nutrients from sunlight. And so far, this green sea slug is the only known animal that can be truly considered solar-powered, although some animals do exhibit some plant-like behaviors. Many scientists have studied the green sea slugs to confirm that they are actually able to create energy from sunlight.

In fact, the slugs use the genetic material so well that they pass it on to their future generations. Their babies retain the ability to produce their own chlorophyll, though they can't generate energy from sunlight until they've eaten enough algae to steal the necessary genes, which they can't yet produce on their own.

"There's no way on earth that genes from an alga should work inside an animal cell," says Sidney Pierce from the University of South Florida. "And yet here, they do. They allow the animal to rely on sunshine for its nutrition. So if something happens to their food source, they have a way of not starving to death until they find more algae to eat."

The sea slugs are so good at gathering energy from the sun that they can live up to nine months without having to eat any food. They get all their nutritional needs met by the genes that they've hijacked from the algae.
